newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Former president contests Madagascar poll result.
newsitem.headline: Former president contests Madagascar poll result.

text.p: Former president Albert Zafy on Monday contested election results that gave former military ruler Didier Ratsiraka an unbeatable lead in the race for the presidency of Madagascar.
According to results from the interior ministry, Ratsiraka had 50.52 of the vote against Zafy's 49.48 percent, leaving the 60-year-old former military ruler 32,000 votes ahead.
There are only some 30,000 votes left to be counted.
Zafy told a news conference he demanded a recount of results from the December 29 second round run-off election, saying some interior ministry officials were allied with Ratsiraka's party.
He said he had proof that the vote counting was rigged but did not want all results cancelled, only those that were issued by the National Electoral Committee since December 31.
Zafy supporters booed journalists at the news conference who asked hostile questions. The president of the journalists' association called for the media to be allowed to do their jobs.
The final results will probably be announced on Wednesday.

Zafy's supporters last week accused officials of manipulating results in favour of Ratsiraka, a retired admiral and a former Marxist who ruled Madagascar for 16 years before losing to Zafy in the last presidential election in 1993.
The High Consitutitonal Court has to approve the results.
Election observers from the Organisation of African Unity, the International Committee of Jurists and the Francophone Agency for Technical and Cultural Cooperation have said the election was normal.
The two-round presidential election was ordered after the National Assembly impeached Zafy, president since 1993, for contravening the constitution and exceeding his powers.
Zafy won the 1993 election after political unrest and subsequent repression paralysed the country for months.
Ratsiraka returned from 19 months in voluntary exile in France to contest the election after Zafy's impeachment.
Ratsiraka campaigned on promises of establishing a "humanistic and ecological republic" in Madagascar, the world's fourth largest island where 14 million people live in chronic poverty.
Political squabbling under Zafy since 1993 in the former French colony has frustrated plans to improve life for the islanders.
